info.title: Koru API Gateway
info.description: The single public API for Koru product clients. Store and AI operations preserve their domain wire contracts behind one authenticated gateway.

runBearer.description: A run's endpoint token, issued once per attempt by POST /v1/artifacts/authorities and rotated by POST /v1/artifacts/authorities/{run}/generation.

code.description: A stable token to branch on.

message.description:
Untranslated developer text; **never shown** to a person. Render your
own words, in your own language, from the code.

waiting_on.description:
Display names of the devices a parked blob hydration is waiting on.
Display data for the client's own sentence — never part of `code`, and
absent on every failure that is not a parked hydration.

hold.description:
**Why blob transfer is holding**, when that is what refused this — a
`TransferHold` code from the blob engine's registry
(`mode_refuses_transport`, `network_metered`, `network_low_data`,
`network_offline`, `paused_by_person`, `cloud_access_unavailable`).

Structured beside `code` rather than inside it, for the same reason
`waiting_on` is: these are the *blob plane's* vocabulary and `code` is
the Store's, and a client that had to recover one by parsing the other
would be branching on developer text. Without it, every hold that is
not one of the Store's three blob codes arrives as `storage_failed`
and the placeholder has nothing true to say — which is D259's second
defect exactly: a person told to wake another device for a Workspace
this one was never switched on for.

Absent on every failure that is not a blob transfer hold.

Failure.description:
The body of every failed request.

`code` is a stable machine-readable token a client branches on. `message` is
**untranslated developer text** that a client must never show to a person —
it is for logs and bug reports. A client renders its own words, in its own
language, from the code.

capabilities.description:
A coarse feature list a client negotiates against, rather than deducing
what a store can do from a version number.

channel.description: Which store this is. Channels never share a database.

started_at.description: Epoch milliseconds. A number, so no calendar or locale is baked in.

StoreBackup.description:
`POST /v1/backup`.

A destination rather than bytes: a whole Store can be large, and the
daemon is the process that can take a consistent snapshot while it holds
the live Store lock. The route is authenticated and loopback-only.

purpose.description: Free text the person chose — "work", "school". Not an enum: it is theirs.

avatar.description:
**A token, never a colour value and never a path.** `color:<name>` today;
`blob:<hash>` when a person can upload a picture. The prefix is what
makes that addition free — a reader splits on the first colon and
branches — where a bare `purple` would have needed a migration.

The store never interprets it. A client maps `color:purple` back to
whatever purple is in the theme it is drawing, which is what keeps one
theme's rendering of a colour out of the person's profile.

icon.description:
Emoji and named tile colour used by profile switchers. Kept separate
from `avatar` so a profile can have both an icon and a colour.

account.description:
Exact `koru:<canonical-v4-identity-uuid>` after acknowledged attachment;
`None` while local-only. Never an email or provider subject.

locale.description: BCP 47. Belongs to the person, never to their content.

kind.description:
Persona or legacy compatibility holder. See [`ProfileKind`].

`#[serde(default)]` keeps profiles written before the field readable.
Current creation always writes `Normal`.

Profile.description:
A persona, not a folder: "Steven — Work", "Steven — Personal".

**Creating one requires no login.** [`Profile::account`] remains `None`
until an explicit compare-and-set binds a hosted Koru Identity. A `ProfileId`
remains distinct from account identity and content identity never changes.

A legacy `Holder` row can still be decoded for migration compatibility,
but current code creates personas only.

Locale.description: A BCP 47 language tag, checked structurally rather than against a registry. Stored canonically: language lowercase, script title case, region uppercase. `und` means undetermined — the absence of an answer, which is not the same as English.

Timestamp.description: Epoch milliseconds, UTC. Signed, so instants before 1970 are representable.

oneOf.description: A persona a person made. Everything a profile can do, it can do.

A legacy non-persona row retained only for schema-lineage compatibility.
It must never become active or appear in a persona selector.

ProfileKind.description:
Compatibility classification for catalog rows.

`Holder` was written by an unreleased dev schema-9 lineage. The merged
catalog preserves and decodes it so those databases migrate safely, but no
production flow creates a holder. Any legacy holder row is excluded from
persona surfaces.

locale.description:
BCP 47. Absent means undetermined — **not** English: the absence of an
answer is not an answer.

It is the **person's** locale, not the language a client happens to be
drawing in: a client with no Korean strings showing English to a `ko-KR`
person still sends `ko-KR`, or the profile records something untrue and
stays wrong on the day Korean arrives.

purpose.description: Free text — "work", "school". Deliberately not an enum: it is theirs.

avatar.description:
A token, `<kind>:<value>` — `color:purple` today, `blob:<hash>` when a
person can upload a picture. Passed through unread.

ClearProfileAccount.description:
Compare-and-clear request used when a hosted-deleted Profile is explicitly
kept as an offline-only local Profile.

LocalProfileRemoval.description:
`DELETE /v1/profiles/{id}/local`.

Both outcomes mean the catalog marker is durable: retries do not turn an
acknowledged write into a not-found error. Settings cleanup is outside this
Store response, while clients can still distinguish the first marker write.

PersonalAttributesResponse.description:
What both personal-attribute routes answer: the entity in its canonical
spelling, and every attribute it carries for the requesting profile. An
unset attribute is an absent key, never a null.

oneOf.description: Free text.
A finite number.

A boolean. Stored only when set — "false" is a value, "unset" is an
absent key.

A calendar date, `YYYY-MM-DD`. Deliberately **not** an instant: it
names a day, the same day in every timezone.

A wall-clock date and time with **no zone**, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`.

The normal shape for a personal timed value, and why it is: `koru.plan`
answers *when do I intend to work on this*, and 09:00 means 09:00
wherever the person wakes up. Pinning it to the zone they were sitting
in when they typed it would make a plan move overnight on a flight —
a decision nobody made.

There is no `tz` field, so nothing can half-fill one.

An instant in epoch milliseconds UTC **plus** the IANA zone it was
meant in (`America/New_York`) — a name rather than an offset, because
daylight-saving rules change what a future offset will be.

The zone is **not optional**: a personal value that is genuinely tied
to a place says which, and one that is not is
[`DatetimeFloating`](Self::DatetimeFloating) instead.

PersonalAttributeValue.description:
A typed personal attribute value.

**The three temporal types are three variants**, and none of them is
"an instant with an optional zone" ([ADR-183]). The meaning is carried by
which variant it is, never by whether a field happens to be filled in, so
there is no reading of a stored value that could go two ways.

[ADR-183]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-206-timemodel--koru-has-three-temporal-types-not-one-with-a-nullable-timezone

SetPersonalAttribute.description:
`PUT /v1/profiles/{id}/personal-attributes`.

One write: set `key` on `entity` to `value`, or clear it when `value` is
null or absent. A cleared attribute is deleted, so reading it back finds
no key at all.

PrivateState.description:
What a reader sees: their private attributes by node, and a revision that
grows with every effective change. Absent state is empty at revision 0.

ApplyPrivateChanges.description:
`PATCH /v1/profiles/{id}/documents/{document}/private-state`.

A bounded batch of explicit values for one reader's private view of one
document. Each change names the value it wants — never "invert" — so a
retried request is a no-op. All or nothing: one invalid change rejects the
batch and applies none of it.

PrivateChange.description:
One requested change: set `key` on `node_id` to `value`, or clear it when
`value` is `null`.

StoredReminder.description:
One reminder as read from the synchronized profile root.

Actions are already scoped by the reminder's child map. The id is still
checked while decoding, so a malformed value cannot escape under a key
naming a different reminder.

PersonalDictionaryResponse.description:
`GET /v1/profiles/{id}/dictionary`, and every write's echo.

The personal spelling dictionary: language tag → sorted words. Personal
state — it replicates between this person's devices and nobody else's.

LocalTime.description: Canonical `HH:MM:SS` wall time. It carries no date and no zone.

SettingsPatch.description:
Patch semantics preserve independent CRDT settings fields. An absent field
is unchanged; `end_of_day: null` explicitly clears that setting.

ReminderQuery.description:
Device context is mandatory for missed/upcoming queries. It is explicit so
a remote caller is never classified through the gateway machine's zone.

source_location.description:
Root-first workspace/document location of the source object. This is
Store-to-desktop presentation data and never crosses the Agent wire.

ReminderTarget.description:
The projection half of one reminder row. `projected = false` means missing
is not authoritative yet; consumers request/retry after the workspace sweep.

OccurrenceSource.description: Canonical source injected by the model-aware projection edge.

OccurrenceMoment.description:
The canonical occurrence moment. A floating moment remains a wall clock;
a zoned moment remains one instant plus one semantic IANA zone.

SetDictionaryWord.description:
`PUT /v1/profiles/{id}/dictionary`.

One write: add `word` to `language`'s set when `present`, remove it
otherwise. A removed word is a deleted key, so reading back finds no word
at all.

icon.description:
How the workspace appears in a switcher: a picture, a colour, and the two
flags that decide where it sits in the list.

**Stored as tokens, never as rendered values.** `icon` is an emoji or a
`blob:<hash>`; `color` is one of the app's colour *names*, not `#6B4FC4`.
Writing a hex value would freeze one theme's purple into somebody's
workspace for good — the same rule onboarding follows for `avatar` and
`purpose` ([ADR-82](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-076-100.md#adr-82-i18n--internationalization-constrains-what-is-stored-not-how-it-is-shown)).

The store never interprets any of them. They are here because they have
to survive a restart and the store is the only thing that persists — the
app's `ProfileDoc` is a view rebuilt from this every launch, so a flag
written only there was written to a cache.

deleted_at.description:
Soft deletion is independent of archive. The Store keeps every byte
until retention purges it, and restoring clears only this timestamp.

position.description:
Stable position in the owner's workspace list. The list may still group
pinned, archived and deleted rows; this orders rows within those groups.

Workspace.description:
The unit of export, backup and — later — sharing.

The same logical workspace may exist as several physical replicas: one per
release channel, one per machine, one in the cloud. They share [`id`] and
**never share a database file**.

[`id`]: Workspace::id

entries.description: Every user-visible manifest entry, across every application kind.

kinds.description:
Counts by application-defined kind token. The Store does not decide
whether `page`, `file`, or a future token is called a document in a UI.

stored_bytes.description:
Deduplicated bytes referenced by live first-class file entries,
excluding embedded note media, Trash, retained recovery data, database
allocation and backups.

WorkspaceUsage.description:
`GET /v1/profiles/{id}/workspace-usage`.

Live file storage is one number on purpose. A caller needs to answer how
much content the visible file set represents, not expose retained recovery
data or the persistence engine's page allocation.

workspaces.description: The complete ordered set, including archived and softly deleted rows.

MoveWorkspace.description:
`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/move`.

**The destination only.** The profile the workspace is leaving is not sent:
the Store already knows it, and a caller that had to name it could name the
wrong one — which would either be ignored, making the field a lie, or
refused, making a move fail because a listing was a moment stale. The field
is spelled `owner` because that is what a workspace's profile is called
everywhere else on this wire, [`NewWorkspace`] included.

WorkspaceAppearance.description:
`PATCH /v1/workspaces/{id}/appearance`.

**All four, every time.** They are edited together and the caller knows all
of them, so sending them whole sidesteps the *absent versus null* question a
partial update has to answer in JSON — and which nobody answers the same way
twice.

ordinal.description:
Position among siblings. Data, not list position, so a reorder is a
field change rather than a structural rewrite.

kind.description:
The application's own kind — "page", "task-list", whatever it defines.
A stable token, and the store never interprets it.

mime.description:
MIME type for opaque file entries. Mirrored into the manifest so a
listing can choose an icon without opening the document snapshot.

note.description:
The note attached to a file, as its document id. `Some` only on a file
that has one; the note itself is an ordinary document registered as the
file's child, so the trash and the purge already follow it.

trashed_at.description:
When this document was put in the trash, if it was.

**Deleting a document is a move, not a delete**
([ADR-69](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-051-075.md#adr-69--trashing-a-document-is-a-move-into-a-hidden-library-node-and-nothing-ever-purges-it)): losing content is the one
unrecoverable bug, so *Move to trash* sets this and nothing else. The
entry stays, its bytes stay, and it is absent from a listing only because
whoever draws the listing filters on this field.

A timestamp rather than a `bool` because the answer to "when did this go"
is worth having and costs the same, and because a sweep that empties the
trash on age has something to sort on if one is ever wanted. Nothing
purges on a timer today.

`#[serde(default)]` so a manifest written before this existed reads as
*not trashed*, which is the truth about every document in it.

trashed_by.description:
A self-declared display label for whoever binned it — "Steven", an email,
whatever the profile says. `None` is normal.

**A label, not an identity.** The store does not resolve it, compare it,
or believe it: it exists so a Trash listing can say *who* without the
window having to look up a profile that may belong to another machine.
Anything that needed to *trust* this would need a `ProfileId` and a way
to verify it, which is a different feature.

DocumentEntry.description: One document as its workspace lists it: identity, where it sits among its siblings, its title and kind, and whether it is in the trash. Listing a workspace opens none of its documents.

DocumentId.description: DocumentId — a client-minted v4 UUID, hyphenated and lowercase. Immutable, and never derived from a name or a path.

DocumentLocation.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/location`.

A document id is globally unique, but opening it still needs the profile and
workspace which own it. Legacy Koru pills predate routed references and
carry only this id; this response lets a client upgrade that old reference
at the boundary where the authoritative catalog lives.

projected.description:
Whether the read model has seen this document at all.

**An empty list means two different things and a caller must be able to
tell them apart.** The projector is debounced, so a heading typed a
moment ago is not here yet; `projected: false` is "still indexing" and
`projected: true` with no headings is "this document has none".

DocumentOutline.description:
`GET /v1/documents/{id}/outline`.

The headings of one document, for a picker offering jump targets. Answered
from the derived read model rather than the document itself, because a
picker must not pay a CRDT decode per keystroke.

node.description:
Meaningful only inside the document that minted it, which is why this
response names that document.

id.description:
Optional client-minted identity. Importers use this so snapshots can
contain routed references to other entries in the same batch.

kind.description:
The application's own kind — `page`, `task-list`. A stable token, and
the store never interprets it.

mime.description:
MIME type for file entries. Optional for ordinary documents and older
clients.

index.description:
Where among `parent`'s children it goes. **Absent means the end**, which
is what every caller with no opinion sends and what an older client's
body decodes as.

The same coordinate `MoveDocument` uses — an index among siblings,
counting the trashed ones, because that is what the manifest tree holds.
Past the end is clamped rather than refused: a new page below the last
one is an ordinary request, not an arithmetic mistake.

trashed_at.description:
Create the manifest row already in Trash at this source timestamp.
Absent preserves the pre-capability behavior for older clients.

snapshot.description:
Optional complete initial state. Used by importers so registering the
manifest row and committing content is one Store operation rather than
a briefly visible empty page followed by a client update.

id.description:
The note's document id — the existing one when the file already had a
note.

created.description: Whether this call created the note.

EnsuredFileNote.description:
What `POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/documents/{document}/note` answers with.

[`Created`] would lose the one fact the caller cannot otherwise learn:
whether this call made the note or the file already had one. The store
reports it — `created` is its answer, not an inference from the delta —
so the answer carries it through unchanged.

index.description: Entry index among siblings under `parent`. Past the end means append.

TransferDocuments.description:
`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/transfer` — move a document (and its explore
subtree) into another workspace in the same store, preserving document ids.

Transferred.description: What a transfer answers with: every document id that moved, root first.

ManifestRef.description:
`GET /v1/workspaces/{id}/manifest` — the document a client joins to see what
a workspace contains.

stale.description:
Whether the document has changed since its newest marker — **the
store's own comparison**, not something a client derives.

A property of the *document*, so it is on the page rather than on each
entry: "changed since the newest marker" is one question however many
rows the page carries.

**`Option`, not `bool`, and that is the whole compatibility story.** A
bare `bool` with `#[serde(default)]` reads `false` — *not stale* — from
every store built before this field existed, and a client that believed
it would offer to rename a marker over a document that has moved on.
`None` means *this store does not say*, and a caller must then fall back
to whatever it did before it could ask.

`Some(true)` when the document has no markers at all: there is nothing
to be unchanged relative to.

HistoryEntryId.description: HistoryEntryId — a client-minted v4 UUID, hyphenated and lowercase. Immutable, and never derived from a name or a path.

DocumentVersionId.description: DocumentVersionId — a client-minted v4 UUID, hyphenated and lowercase. Immutable, and never derived from a name or a path.

reason.description:
One of the `HistoryReason` tokens. Public captures normally use
`manual`; MCP and restore use their paired boundary reasons.

RelabelHistory.description:
Rename a history marker. `label: None` clears the name; the marker then
falls back to its reason in every listing.

filename.description:
The name the person's file had. **Metadata only** — arbitrary Unicode,
never identity, never a path component, never emitted into a header
unencoded.

attributes.description:
Typed extra facts, keyed by a `blob_attr` constant. Additive on the
wire and in storage: absent reads as empty, and an unknown key is kept
but ignored.

Blob.description:
What the CRDT references, and what the catalog records.

The bytes are never in Loro; this is.

BlobHash.description:
`<algorithm>:<digest>` — `b3:<64 hex>`.

The algorithm is in the value because a hash that does not say what it is
cannot be migrated: adopting a second one has to be additive, or every
document already written is orphaned.

oneOf.description:
One of a fixed set of tokens, spelled in the key's documentation —
the same rule as every other enum in this file.

BlobAttribute.description:
A typed value in a [`Blob`]'s attribute map.

The map is the extension point: a new fact about a blob is a new key, never
a new column, so adding one does not touch the schema, the wire framing or
older readers (they ignore keys they do not know). Values stay typed so a
reader never has to guess whether `"7"` is a number.

AssociateBlob.description:
`POST /v1/workspaces/{id}/blobs/{hash}` — associate another workspace owned
by the same Profile with one content-addressed blob.

A selection moved across workspaces carries blob references in its CRDT
cutting, and the target must be associated before those references are
published or it holds a reference it may not read.

**Named for the association rather than a copy**, because no bytes move:
one stored object serves every workspace associated with it, and the
association is the permission. The old name described a layout that filed
one picture once per workspace, and a caller that still believes it would
duplicate a picture library across workspaces.

workspaces.description:
Which workspaces to search. Empty means every workspace this store
holds.

has.description:
Only nodes carrying this attribute key (`koru.due`, or a custom
definition's key).

missing.description:
Only nodes **not** carrying this key. Combined with the base rule this
reads "has some attribute, but not this one".

tags.description:
Only nodes carrying any of these tags, each a `TagId` in storage form.
Ids, never names — the tag table owns names and rename must not change
what a saved query matches.

priority.description:
Only nodes whose `koru.priority` equals this token
(`low | medium | high | urgent`).

min_priority.description:
Only nodes whose `koru.priority` is this token or more important —
the semantic order `low < medium < high < urgent`, never the
alphabetic one.

due.description: Which `koru.due` values match, **stated per temporal type**.

sort.description:
`due`, `priority` or `modified`. Absent means `modified` — newest
first, which is what a surface with no opinion wants.

group_by.description:
Ask for **corpus-wide counts** beside the page. `tag` is the only
token; absent means no groups, and the response's `groups` is empty.

It is a separate question from paging, deliberately: a client can count
a page itself, and what it cannot do is count the rows it did not
fetch. So the counts come from their own statement over the same
filter, and a group's count is the whole matching corpus rather than
the page above it.

limit.description:
Rows per page. Absent means the server default; the server also caps
it, so a huge number is a full page rather than a full table.

offset.description: Rows to skip. Page by increasing this until a short page comes back.

AttributeQuery.description:
`POST /v1/attributes/query`.

Every filter is optional and absent means "no constraint". Filters
compose with AND; the values inside `tags` compose with OR (any of).
The base set is nodes carrying **at least one attribute** — a bare
paragraph is never a row of an attribute query, even under `missing`.

dates.description:
Compared against dues stored as a **calendar date** — and against
floating wall clocks, whose day needs no zone to read.

instants.description: Compared against dues stored as a **zoned instant**.

DueFilter.description:
Which due values match, **one window per temporal type** ([ADR-183]).

Koru stores three temporal types and never one with a nullable timezone, so
a filter says which of them it is asking about. The windows compose with
**OR** — "everything due this week, however it was set" is genuinely two
questions asked of two kinds of value — and a row of a type this filter did
not name simply does not match.

What this deliberately does **not** do is fold one type onto the other. The
shape it replaced took a single bound and cut instants at the UTC day
boundary, which is wrong by a day for a third of the planet: 15:00Z on
September 2 is already September 3 in Tokyo. A caller that wants a
zone-exact window computes its own millisecond edges, because the caller is
the layer that knows which zone the person is asking in.

Naming neither window is refused: it is a question nobody asked, and
answering "everything" would be a guess.

[ADR-183]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-206-timemodel--koru-has-three-temporal-types-not-one-with-a-nullable-timezone

DateWindow.description:
A half-open calendar window, `[after, before)`. Each bound is strictly
`YYYY-MM-DD`; absent means unbounded on that side.

InstantWindow.description:
A half-open instant window, `[after_ms, before_ms)`, in epoch milliseconds
UTC. Absent means unbounded on that side.

rows.description: The matching nodes, one row each, in the requested order.

definitions.description:
Every attribute definition in play: the system registry always, plus
the scoped workspaces' custom definitions — so a filter UI builds its
controls from types rather than guessing.

tags.description:
The scoped workspaces' tag tables (live tags only, merge tombstones
resolved away), so a `koru.tag` value — a `TagId` — resolves to a name
and a chip color without another request.

groups.description:
Corpus-wide counts per tag, when the query asked for them with
`group_by`. Empty otherwise.

**Names are not repeated here**: a group carries the `TagId` and the
count, and `tags` above is where that id becomes a word and a color.
Two spellings of one name in one response is a drift waiting to happen.

projected.description:
Whether every workspace in scope has reached the read model at all.
`false` is "still indexing" — the projector is debounced, so an
attribute set a moment ago may not be a row yet.

updating_workspaces.description:
The workspaces the answer may be behind on, by the same rule search
uses: named rather than waited for.

limit.description: The page size actually applied, after the server's cap.

node.description: The node id, meaningful only inside `document`.

excerpt.description:
The node's text, truncated to a bounded number of characters —
characters, never bytes, so no language is cut mid-glyph.

document_title.description: The source document's title, from the workspace listing.

trashed.description:
Whether the source document sits in the trash, **inherited down the
document tree** — a child of a binned parent carries no stamp of its
own. Trashed rows are flagged, never hidden: restore must be able to
find them.

attributes.description:
Every attribute on the node — not only the ones the filter named, so a
row can be drawn without a second request.

AttributeRow.description:
One matching node. The identity is `(workspace, document, node)`, carried
together — never a node id on its own.

id.description: The attr record's own id, stable across edits to its value.

role.description:
The attribute key the value is stored under — `koru.due`, `koru.tag`,
or a custom definition's key.

zone.description:
The IANA zone a `datetime_zoned` value was meant in, and absent for
every other kind.

It travels with the instant rather than being dropped as presentation:
a consumer handed an epoch-ms number alone would be holding the
ambiguous shape the three types exist to abolish. Which zone a reader
*displays* it in is that consumer's own, separate decision.

AttributeRowValue.description:
One attribute on one row, as the projection carries it: the value's shape
in `kind` and its canonical string in `value`.

`kind` is one of `date`, `datetime_floating`, `datetime_zoned`, `number`,
`bool`, `ref`, `url`, `text` — **three temporal tokens, and no `datetime`
that might be either** ([ADR-183]). `value` is the canonical string for
that kind: a calendar date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, a floating wall clock as
`YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS`, a zoned instant as decimal epoch-ms, a tag as its
`TagId`.

[ADR-183]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-206-timemodel--koru-has-three-temporal-types-not-one-with-a-nullable-timezone

id.description:
Stable identity: the namespaced key itself for a system attribute, a
generated UUID for a custom one. Rename never changes it.

key.description: The key values are stored under.

value_type.description:
`text`, `number`, `boolean`, `date`, `datetime_zoned`,
`datetime_floating`, `select`, `multi_select`.

**The definition declares which temporal type the key takes.** A shared
key such as `koru.due` is `datetime_zoned` and refuses a floating
value; a personal one such as `koru.plan` is `datetime_floating` and
refuses a zoned one ([ADR-183]).

scope.description:
`shared | personal`. Personal values never appear in this response's
rows — they live per profile, not on nodes.

options.description:
The legal tokens for a select; empty otherwise, and empty for
`koru.tag`, whose options are the tag table.

AttributeDefinition.description:
One attribute definition, flattened to tokens. The same shape for the
compiled-in system registry and a workspace's custom records; `system`
says which this is.

id.description: The `TagId`, which is what node attributes store.

color.description: An accent color token, or absent for the default chip.

workspace.description:
Which workspace's table this row is from — tags are workspace-scoped,
and a multi-workspace query returns each table's rows.

AttributeTag.description: One live tag from a scoped workspace's tag table.

workspace.description: Which workspace's tag table names this id.

tag.description: The `TagId` in storage form. Look it up in `tags` for a name and color.

count.description:
Distinct nodes carrying it across the whole matching corpus — not the
page. A node with two tags counts once in each group, so the counts sum
to more than `rows.len()` even on a complete page.

trashed.description:
How many of `count` sit in a binned document. Binned rows are counted
and flagged rather than dropped, exactly as they are in `rows` — a
heading that hid them would disagree with the list underneath it.

AttributeGroup.description:
One tag's share of the whole matching corpus.

**Keyed by `(workspace, tag)`**, because a `TagId` belongs to one
workspace's table and the `tags` array is per table too. A multi-workspace
query gets a group per table rather than one merged heading.

**The id is the one a live table can name.** A tag merged into another
re-points no node ([ADR-176]), so nodes go on carrying the merged-away id;
the store folds those counts into the surviving tag before answering, so a
merge shows as one group rather than splitting into a named half and a
nameless one. The consequence worth knowing: the id here is not necessarily
an id any row's `koru.tag` value spells.

[ADR-176]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-176-200.md#adr-176-consenton--telemetry-consent-defaults-on-and-a-discoverable-opt-out-is-what-buys-it

workspaces.description:
Which workspaces to search. Empty means every workspace this store
holds.

has.description:
Only tasks carrying this attribute key (`koru.due`, or a custom
definition's key).

tags.description:
Only tasks carrying any of these tags, each a `TagId` in storage form.
Ids, never names — the tag table owns names and rename must not change
what a saved query matches.

priority.description:
Only tasks whose `koru.priority` equals this token
(`low | medium | high | urgent`).

min_priority.description:
Only tasks whose `koru.priority` is this token or more important — the
semantic order `low < medium < high < urgent`, never the alphabetic one.

due.description: Which `koru.due` values match, **stated per temporal type**.

bucket.description:
Only tasks in **one agenda bucket** — `today`, `next`, `upcoming`,
`later` or `completed` (SPEC §7).

Usable **only with [`bucket_windows`](Self::bucket_windows)**, which is
where the reader's zone was resolved; naming one without the other is a
400, as is a token that is not one of the five. A bucket is never
persisted and never guessed — a store that invented today's date would
be wrong by morning and wrong in another country.

**A bucket names a lifecycle, so it supersedes
[`lifecycle`](Self::lifecycle).** `Completed` is one of the five and the
other four are open by rule 1 of the bucket function, so ANDing the two
fields would answer `bucket: "completed"` with an empty page under the
*default* lifecycle — a silent trap on the most obvious request. When
this field is present, the query's `lifecycle` is not applied.

bucket_windows.description:
The reader's zone, already resolved into days and instants — required by
[`bucket`](Self::bucket) and by `group_by: "bucket"`.

completed_on_or_after.description:
**Hide tasks completed before this day** — a canonical `YYYY-MM-DD`,
inclusive, which the caller computed from its own today and
[`COMPLETED_WINDOW_DAYS`].

It applies to completed rows and to nothing else, so it narrows the
Completed queue and leaves the four open ones exactly as they were.

**A task the store cannot date is kept.** A completion recorded before
this build carries no day, and a store that cannot tell how old
something is must not call it old: hiding those would take work out of
sight that nobody could ask for back. They age out as they are
reopened, finished again, or taken off Tasks.

recently_completed_since.description:
**Keep tasks completed on or after this day where they were**, rather
than only in the Completed queue: a canonical `YYYY-MM-DD` the caller
computed from its own today.

What it loosens is *where a completed task is listed*, not what a task
is. A queue places a row by its due when this covers it, so something
ticked this morning stays on the page it was ticked on, struck
through, instead of vanishing; a list shows it beside the open work in
it. Nothing else about the row changes, and the row is still in the
Completed queue as well — the two pages are two questions.

**The counts do not carry it**, deliberately: a queue's number is how
much open work is in it, and ticking something should make that number
go down rather than leave it where it was.

list.description:
Only tasks in this list — a `ListId` in storage form.

**A list is a filter, not a place** (SPEC §8): membership is one
`koru.list` value on the task, so this is one more predicate over one
more attribute and ANDs with every filter above it. Ids, never names —
the workspace's list table owns names, and renaming a list must not
change what a saved query matches. An id no table names matches nothing.

group_by.description:
Ask for **corpus-wide counts** beside the page. `list` or `bucket`;
absent means no groups, and the response's `groups` is empty. An unknown
token is a 400, never a silently ungrouped answer.

The attribute query's rule, applied here: a client can count a page
itself, and what it cannot do is count the rows it did not fetch — so a
sidebar's "14" comes from its own statement over the same filter rather
than from the page above it.

`bucket` requires [`bucket_windows`](Self::bucket_windows) and answers
**five rows per workspace**, one per bucket — the rail's
*Today 5 · 3 overdue, Next 12, Upcoming 40, Later 9, Completed 118*. It
partitions by lifecycle (`Completed` is one of the five), so it does not
apply [`lifecycle`](Self::lifecycle) either, for
[`bucket`](Self::bucket)'s reason.

overdue.description:
**Which dues count as overdue**, stated per temporal type — used only to
split `groups`, never to filter rows.

Overdue is a fact about the reader's display zone (SPEC §7) and the
store carries no timezone database, so the caller computes the windows
and sends them: typically `dates.before = today` and
`instants.before_ms = now`. Absent means every group's `overdue` is
zero, which is the honest answer to a question nobody asked.

lifecycle.description:
Open, completed, or both. Absent means open — a task list answers *what
should I do next*, and absence of `koru.task_state` is itself `open`.

include_trashed.description:
Also return tasks sitting in their document's own bin, each flagged with
[`TaskRow::in_trash`]. Off by default; on is how a binned task stays
restorable from a Tasks surface.

It does **not** govern binned *documents*: those rows are always
returned, flagged with [`TaskRow::document_trashed`].

sort.description:
`due`, `priority` or `modified`. Absent means `due` — soonest first,
undated last.

limit.description: Rows per page, clamped by the store; see [`MAX_LIMIT`].

after.description:
The `task:` reference the previous page ended on, exclusive.

**Keyset, never an offset.** A Tasks view re-queries at every local
midnight and on every resume, and an offset page silently repeats or
skips a row when anything inserts above it. A reference that no longer
matches the filter is not an error: the answer comes from the top with
[`TaskQueryResponse::restarted`] set.

covering.description:
**Writes this answer must include** for the caller to trust it.

A surface that has just written a document and re-asks the read model
can be answered from a projection that has not seen the write yet — the
store projects asynchronously and coalesces. Naming the write lets the
answer say so through [`TaskQueryResponse::covered`], and the caller can
ask again rather than draw a number it knows is behind.

**Optional and additive.** Absent means the caller is not waiting on
anything; an older client never sends it. At most
[`MAX_COVERING`] entries; a malformed one refuses the request rather
than answering *uncovered*, because a malformed requirement is a client
bug and a quiet answer would hide it. Pagination is untouched.

TaskQuery.description:
`POST /v1/tasks/query`.

Every filter is optional and absent means "no constraint". Filters compose
with AND; the values inside `tags` compose with OR (any of). The base set is
**derived, never marked in a second table**: a node is a task when it
carries the `koru.task` marker or a due date, which is the whole derivation
([ADR-285]).

[ADR-285]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-276-300.md#adr-285-taskmodel--a-task-is-a-marked-node-and-the-marker-or-a-due-date-is-the-whole-derivation

today.description:
Today in the reader's zone, strictly `YYYY-MM-DD`. A due on or before it
is `Today` — **overdue lands in Today**, because an overdue task is the
answer to *what should I do next*.

horizon.description:
The last day of `Next`, strictly `YYYY-MM-DD` — `today + 7` under the
shipped rule, but the *caller's* arithmetic, not this store's.

upcoming_horizon.description:
The last day of `Upcoming`, strictly `YYYY-MM-DD` — `today + 30` under
the shipped rule. Beyond it is `Later`, which is why one horizon is not
enough to place a row.

today_ends_ms.description:
The instant [`today`](Self::today) ends at in the reader's zone,
epoch-ms UTC: the edge a **zoned** due is compared against for `Today`.

horizon_ends_ms.description: The instant [`horizon`](Self::horizon) ends at, epoch-ms UTC.

upcoming_ends_ms.description:
The instant [`upcoming_horizon`](Self::upcoming_horizon) ends at,
epoch-ms UTC.

now_ms.description:
Now, epoch-ms UTC — what makes a *zoned* due overdue, beside
[`today`](Self::today), which is what makes a dated one overdue.

It splits the counts and never selects a row: an overdue task is in
`Today` either way, and this is what tints it.

min_next_priority.description:
The priority an **undated** task must reach to be `Next` rather than
`Later` — a priority token, `high` under SPEC §7's rule that priority
≥ High replaces the original proposal's *Important*.

On the wire rather than compiled in, for the reason every other window
here is: it is a product rule the caller states, and a store that knew
it would be a second place to change it.

BucketWindows.description:
**The reader's zone, resolved into days and instants by the caller.**

SPEC §7 makes a bucket a pure function of `(due, lifecycle, priority, today,
zone)`, and this store carries no timezone database — so a caller that wants
buckets computes the edges and sends them, exactly as
[`TaskQuery::overdue`] already does for the overdue split. Nothing here is
guessed, defaulted or derived from a server clock: a store that decided what
*today* meant would be wrong by morning and wrong in another country, which
is the whole reason [ADR-287] refused to persist a bucket.

Six edges rather than the two a first sketch has, because the bucket
function has **two** horizons and each of them has to be stated twice:

- a **day** edge, for dues stored as a calendar date or a floating wall
  clock — those carry a day that needs no zone to read;
- an **instant** edge, for dues stored as a zoned instant, whose day is
  `ZonedDateTime::date_in(zone)` and therefore the caller's to compute.

The two are compared each in its own terms and never folded together
([ADR-183] rule 5). Calendar days here are inclusive last days — the day
`Next` ends on, and the day `Upcoming` ends on — because that is how the
domain function reads (*within seven days*, *within thirty*); the instants
are the moments those days **end**, which is the same edge said the other
way.

[ADR-183]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-206-timemodel--koru-has-three-temporal-types-not-one-with-a-nullable-timezone
[ADR-287]: ../../../docs/decisions/ADR-276-300.md#adr-287-taskread--the-tasks-query-is-a-second-question-asked-of-the-one-read-model

LifecycleFilter.description: Which of them a query wants.

TaskSort.description:
What orders the page.

`Due` is the default because a task list is asked *what should I do next*.
`Due` and `Priority` sort set values first and unset last; `Modified` is the
source document's stamp.

peer.description:
The writing session's Loro peer id. A `String` because it is a `u64`
and JSON numbers are `f64` — the id would lose its low bits above 2^53
in any JavaScript client, and these ids are random across the range.

counter.description:
The exclusive end of that peer's own operations when the write
committed. Covered when the projection has applied at least this many
of them.

RevisionRequirement.description:
One write a query wants included — see [`TaskQuery::covering`].

The workspace rides with it: the query's scope is workspaces, and a
document the projector has never seen (the first native task's own
`task-list` document) has no projection row to place it by. Scope is
answered against the workspace, and an unprojected document is simply
*uncovered*.
**A scoped receipt: the one operation the caller is waiting for.**

This used to be the document's whole version vector, and that was a bug
with a delay fuse on it. A version vector holds one entry per writer the
document has ever had, and Loro mints a fresh writer id per session — so
the requirement grew by ~21 hex characters every time any process opened
the document, and once it crossed [`MAX_COVERING`]'s sibling length limit
the store refused **every** task query naming a write. Measured: 100
writers encode to 2 126 hex characters, 200 to 4 220. The surfaces then had
no way to wait, so every optimistic row snapped back — the tick that
un-ticks itself.

What a surface actually needs to know is *has the projection seen my
write*, and that is one operation, not a census of everybody who ever
touched the document. `peer` is the writing session and `counter` is the
**exclusive** end of its own operations at the moment the mutation
committed, which is exactly `VersionVector::get(peer)`.

**Bounded by construction**: two integers, whatever the document's history.
That is the property the old shape could not have at any limit.

**Multi-operation writes need nothing extra.** A command that writes five
operations still ends at one counter, and one peer's operations are
contiguous — so covering the end covers all of them. A command that wrote
nothing produces no receipt at all; see [`TaskQuery::covering`].

rows.description: The matching tasks, one row each, in the requested order.

definitions.description:
Every attribute definition in play: the system registry always, plus the
scoped workspaces' custom definitions — so a surface draws a value from
its type rather than guessing.

tags.description:
The scoped workspaces' tag tables (live tags only, merge tombstones
resolved away), so a `koru.tag` value resolves to a name and a chip
color without another request.

groups.description:
Corpus-wide counts per group — per list, or per bucket — when the query
asked for them with `group_by`. Empty otherwise.

**Names are not repeated here.** A group carries its key — a `ListId`,
or a bucket token — with the count and the overdue share; the name, the
swatch and the rail order live in the workspace's list table, which a
client reads from its own workspace rather than from this response. Two
spellings of one name in one answer is a drift waiting to happen — the
same rule `tags` follows above.

projected.description:
Whether every workspace in scope has reached the read model at all.
`false` is "still indexing" — the projector is debounced, so a task
created a moment ago may not be a row yet.

updating_workspaces.description:
The workspaces the answer may be behind on, by the same rule search and
the attribute query use: **named rather than waited for**.

limit.description: The page size actually applied, after the store's cap.

next_after.description:
The `task:` reference to pass as the next request's
[`TaskQuery::after`], or absent when this page is the end of the list.

restarted.description:
The `after` this request carried named a row the filter no longer
matches — completed, removed or binned between pages — so the answer is
page one again. A client can tell a fresh list from a continuation
instead of silently drawing page one twice.

covered.description:
Whether the rows and counts include every write in
[`TaskQuery::covering`].

**`None` means this server cannot tell** — an older store that never
read the requirement. A client must read `None` as *unknown*, never as
coverage: it records the capability as absent, falls back to its
ordinary schedule and stops sending requirements, so an old server is
never asked again quickly for an answer it cannot give. A server that
understands the field always answers `Some`, `true` when nothing was
required.

A different question from [`projected`](Self::projected), which says
whether the workspace has been indexed at all; both are worth having.

node.description: The node id, meaningful only inside `document`.

task.description:
`task:<workspace>:<document>:<node>` — the row's identity, the cursor a
page ends on, and the subject its activity is filed under.

node_kind.description:
The node's kind token — one of the task-capable kinds `paragraph`,
`task`, `document`, `image`, `file`.

lifecycle.description: `open` or `completed`. Absence of the stored state reads as `open`.

document_trashed.description:
Whether the **document** sits in the trash, inherited down the document
tree. Flagged, never hidden.

in_trash.description:
Whether the **node** sits in its document's own hidden trash root. Rows
like this come back only under [`TaskQuery::include_trashed`].

breadcrumb.description:
Where the task lives: the workspace, then the document path, then the
ancestor rows, joined by `" / "` — one rule, computed the same way by
the desktop from an open document and by the store from the projection.

title.description:
The task's own title: its text, else its authored name, else
"Untitled" — `koru-title`'s one chain.

attributes.description:
Every attribute on the node — not only the ones the filter named, so a
row can be drawn without a second request.

TaskRow.description:
One task. The identity is `(workspace, document, node)`, carried together —
never a node id on its own — and [`task`](Self::task) is the same triple as
the one string that is also its pagination key and its activity subject.

workspace.description: Which workspace this group counts in.

list.description:
**The group's key**, in the vocabulary the query's `group_by` named: a
`ListId` in storage form under `"list"`, one of [`BUCKETS`] under
`"bucket"`.

A list id the table no longer names still counts — a deleted list's
memberships clear document by document, and a stale value is not a
missing task.

The field is spelled `list` because lists were the only grouping when it
was published, and this route's schemas are generated and consumed:
widening the name would break every caller and every literal built
against it for a rename. It wants to be `key`, and that is a rename to
make in one change with its call sites rather than a second field
carrying a second meaning.

count.description: Matching tasks in this group across the whole corpus — not the page.

overdue.description:
How many of `count` are overdue: by the windows the query's `overdue`
named when grouping by list, and by `bucket_windows`' `today` and
`now_ms` when grouping by bucket — one notion of overdue through one SQL
builder, stated once by whichever object the grouping already required.
Zero when nothing named it; dateless tasks are never overdue, and a
completed task is not overdue whatever its due says.

trashed.description:
How many of `count` sit in a binned document. Counted and flagged
rather than dropped, exactly as those rows are.

TaskGroup.description:
One group's share of the whole matching corpus, when a query asked for
counts with `group_by`.

**Keyed by `(workspace, key)`**, because a `ListId` belongs to one
workspace's list table and folding two workspaces' rails together would
name a group neither of them has. A *bucket* key is universal rather than
workspace-scoped, and the rows stay per workspace anyway: a task belongs to
exactly one workspace, so a cross-workspace rail sums them and loses
nothing, while folding here would throw away an answer a client may want.

Under `group_by: "list"` these do not overlap: `koru.list` is
cardinality-one, so a task is in exactly one list or in none, and the counts
sum to at most the number of matching tasks. A list nothing matches has **no
row** rather than a zero — a client draws its rail from the list table and
reads a missing group as an empty bucket. Buckets partition the corpus for
the same reason and completely: every task is in exactly one of the five,
so those counts sum to the whole matching set.

workspaces.description:
Empty means every workspace the index knows. **The caller resolves a
profile to this**; the index has never heard of one.

tags.description:
Tag **names**, not `TagId`s — this is a text-search surface and a
person types the word they read. A hit's node must carry every one of
them, and a name here matches its own descendants too (`fun` matches
`fun/home`), so this is *node-scoped filtering* rather than a term:
nothing here is searched for, ranked, or spelled back in
[`SearchPage::corrected_query`]
([ADR-207](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-207-tagfilter--a-tag-in-a-query-is-a-node-scoped-filter-not-a-term-and-it-lives-in-candidates-alone)).

A surface may fill this directly; a person fills it by typing `#tag`
into [`Self::text`], which the store lifts out before it searches.

attributes.description:
Typed attribute filters. A hit's node must satisfy **every** one.

One general filter rather than a field per attribute, because a
workspace defines its own attributes and declares their types: a wire
naming `priority` and `due` explicitly would need a new field for every
attribute anybody invents, while `key` + `kinds` serves a custom one on
the day it exists.

request_seq.description:
Copied to the response, so a surface typing quickly can drop an answer
to a keystroke it has already moved past.

include_facets.description: Also return the workspaces the index knows, for a scope picker.

recent_queries.description: Also return this many recent queries. Absent means none.

SearchRequest.description:
The body of `POST /v1/search`.

**A body rather than a query string.** The access log records the path and
its query, and the store's logs rotate daily for a week —
`GLOBAL_SEARCH.md` is explicit that query text never enters a document, the
index, settings, telemetry or the recent-query list, and a URL would put it
in the middle of all of them.

key.description: The attribute key: `koru.due`, `koru.priority`, or a workspace's own.

values.description:
The operand(s). Empty for `Exists`/`Missing`, one for `Is`/`Before`/
`After`, two for `Between`, any number for `OneOf`.

numeric_values.description:
The **same operands again, for the kinds that compare as numbers** —
epoch milliseconds for a `datetime_zoned`, the plain number for a
`number`. Positionally identical to [`Self::values`]: same count, same
order, same meaning.

**This exists because one filter names kinds that do not share a
column.** A due window is `["date", "datetime_zoned"]`, and there is
deliberately no column those two could be compared through
([ADR-217](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-217-typedsearch--search-keeps-every-attribute-in-its-declared-type-and-a-filter-names-the-kinds-it-compares-against)): the date
half needs `2026-09-10` and the instant half needs `1789...`. Without a
second operand list the instant half would silently drop out — an ISO
date does not parse as a number — and the filter would answer only for
all-day deadlines while looking as though it answered for both.

Empty means [`Self::values`] applies to every named kind, which is
right whenever they all compare the same way (`/effort >3`).

**The caller computes it, because the caller knows the zone.** Turning
a calendar day into an instant is a zone question, and the store has no
answer to it — the same rule `DueFilter` already states.

kinds.description:
Which stored kinds this applies to. See the type docs — an empty list
matches nothing, deliberately, rather than guessing.

AttrFilter.description:
One typed attribute filter.

**`kinds` is not optional and not a hint.** A stored value is compared only
against a filter that names its kind, which is what keeps the three
temporal types three: a `date` due and a `datetime_zoned` due are different
questions, and a window naming one does not answer the other
([ADR-206](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-206-timemodel--koru-has-three-temporal-types-not-one-with-a-nullable-timezone)). Name every kind
the question covers — a due window usually means `["date",
"datetime_zoned"]` — or the answer silently omits the rest.

Comparison follows the kind: `number` and `datetime_zoned` compare as
numbers, everything else as its canonical text, which is ISO for the
remaining temporal kinds and therefore ordered correctly within one kind.

oneOf.description: Equal to the single value.
Equal to any of the values.
Strictly less than the single value.
Greater than or equal to the single value.
`[values[0], values[1])`.
Carries this key at all, whatever the value.
Does not carry this key.

AttrOp.description:
How an [`AttrFilter`] compares.

Ranges are **half-open**, matching the windows the attribute service
already uses: `Before` is `< value`, `After` is `>= value`, and `Between`
is `[first, second)`. A person asking for "before the 10th" does not mean
the 10th, and one asking for "after the 10th" does.

LifecycleFilter2.description: Which of them a query wants.

SearchResponse.description:
What `POST /v1/search` answers.

**One round trip, not three.** A search surface wants the page, the scope
picker's list and the recent queries on the same keystroke; the two extras
are optional and off by default, so a caller that only wants hits pays for
hits.

updating_workspaces.description:
Workspaces the answer may be behind on — not yet compared against the
store since it came up, or with indexing still queued. **Reported rather
than waited on**: a query that blocked until every workspace was current
would be correct and occasionally unbounded.

corrected_query.description:
A corrected spelling inferred from the highest-ranked result. Absent
when the authored query itself supplied the evidence.

document.description: Absent when the hit is the workspace itself.

document_kind.description:
Kind of the containing manifest entry. Unlike `kind`, this remains
`file` when the matching fragment is its mirrored title.

mime.description: MIME type of an opaque file, when the manifest recorded one.

title.description: The document's name, from the listing.

breadcrumb.description:
Workspace and the document's title path, assembled at query time —
**never stored**, so renaming a document is one row and re-indexes
nothing.

observed_modified_at_ms.description:
When this store last observed **different** searchable content for the
containing document. Derived local metadata, not an authored timestamp,
and deliberately not *when we last looked*.

workspace_last_used_at_ms.description: Most recent navigation into this workspace on this machine.

MatchSpan.description:
UTF-8 byte offsets in the string they explain.

**Bytes, not characters.** The text they index into is UTF-8, and a surface
slicing it needs the same units it will slice with.

Lifecycle.description:
Whether a hit's document is in the trash.

**Not a property of a fragment.** Trash is a flag on the manifest entry
([ADR-95](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-076-100.md#adr-95-trash--a-document-in-the-trash-is-a-flag-on-its-manifest-entry)), so it is a property
of the *document*, resolved by joining the mirrored listing. Storing it on
every fragment is what used to let a hit and its own document title disagree
about whether they were binned.

RecentQuery.description: A query that led somewhere, and when.

query.description: What was typed to get here. Empty is allowed and records nothing.

Navigation.description:
The body of `POST /v1/search/navigated`.

**Machine-local, derived, and never written into a shared profile or a
collaborative document**: it describes this person's activity on this
desktop. A query earns a place in the history only by leading somewhere,
which is why the text arrives here rather than on the search itself.

GatewayStatus.description:
`GET /v1/status`. Its first four fields preserve the Store status shape so
older readers ignore the additive gateway readiness fields safely.

FederatedSearchRequest.description:
The public `POST /v1/search` body. Existing Store-search fields stay at the
top level; federation adds only an opt-out and an opaque continuation.

workspaces.description:
Empty means every workspace the index knows. **The caller resolves a
profile to this**; the index has never heard of one.

tags.description:
Tag **names**, not `TagId`s — this is a text-search surface and a
person types the word they read. A hit's node must carry every one of
them, and a name here matches its own descendants too (`fun` matches
`fun/home`), so this is *node-scoped filtering* rather than a term:
nothing here is searched for, ranked, or spelled back in
[`SearchPage::corrected_query`]
([ADR-207](../../../docs/decisions/ADR-201-225.md#adr-207-tagfilter--a-tag-in-a-query-is-a-node-scoped-filter-not-a-term-and-it-lives-in-candidates-alone)).

A surface may fill this directly; a person fills it by typing `#tag`
into [`Self::text`], which the store lifts out before it searches.

attributes.description:
Typed attribute filters. A hit's node must satisfy **every** one.

One general filter rather than a field per attribute, because a
workspace defines its own attributes and declares their types: a wire
naming `priority` and `due` explicitly would need a new field for every
attribute anybody invents, while `key` + `kinds` serves a custom one on
the day it exists.

request_seq.description:
Copied to the response, so a surface typing quickly can drop an answer
to a keystroke it has already moved past.

ChatId.description: ChatId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

MessageId.description: MessageId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

MessageBlockId.description: MessageBlockId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

message.description: Safe developer-facing detail. Product UI renders localized copy by code.

StreamEvent.description: One normalized event on the public SSE stream.

oneOf.description:
A one-line fact about the attempt the surface shows and nothing
stores: a local agent could not be reattached and a replacement was
started with the conversation so far.

PublicAiEvent.description:
An event safe to expose across Koru's public AI boundary.

Provider tool calls are deliberately absent: their arguments and reasoning
continuity data remain inside the worker. Clients observe only the minimal
[`ToolActivity`] projection: stable target ids and a bounded public failure
summary, never raw tool arguments or results.

InferenceAttemptId.description: InferenceAttemptId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

ReasoningChoice.description: A provider's reasoning setting — `ai.db`'s nine-token CHECK.

agent_label.description:
A local agent's own label for the call (*Read README.md*), bounded,
kept since schema 8 so a row reads the same after the turn as during
it. `None` on Koru's own tool rows.

agent_summary.description:
What a local agent's permission request asked, bounded, kept since
schema 8.

agent_input.description:
What the agent asked the tool to do — a command line, a change's
paths, an MCP call's arguments — bounded to [`crate::AGENT_CONTENT_CHARS`],
kept since schema 8 (UC17).

agent_output.description:
What the tool produced — output, a diff, a result — bounded to
[`crate::AGENT_CONTENT_CHARS`], kept since schema 8 (UC17).

live.description:
A local agent's live state for this row — the choices a pending
permission request offers — populated only from the worker's live
turn table while the turn runs. `None` on every repository read and
after the turn ends. The agent's wording lives on the row's own
`agent_*` fields.

ToolActivity.description:
Durable and public tool activity. Raw arguments, results, queries, titles,
paths, and workspace content deliberately have no field in this type. The
stable target ids and bounded public error summary are the only context kept
for an auditable, useful activity row.

ToolInvocationId.description: ToolInvocationId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

choices.description:
The choices offered for a pending permission request; empty once
answered. The agent's wording for the row — its label, a permission's
summary, the call's input and output — is on the row itself, stored
(schema 8); only the choices, which a person answers once, are live.

AgentActivityLive.description:
The live half of an agent's activity row: shown while the turn runs,
`None` on every repository read and after the turn ends.

OfferedChoice.description:
One option an agent offered for a permission request. `id` is opaque and
scoped to its request; `label` is the agent's own wording, bounded and
live only.

ChoiceIntent.description:
What choosing an offered option means, as the agent classified it. The
surface focuses a rejection first and never picks between two options of
one intent on the person's behalf.

AttemptNotice.description:
A fact about the attempt the surface shows as one line and nothing
stores: the agent could not be reattached and a replacement was started
with the conversation so far.

agents.description:
The local coding agents this AI service can drive, as chat providers
(`agent-<kind>`) with the name a person knows each by. Empty where
no session host exists. Readiness is asked per agent through
validation, like any provider's.

AiProviderId.description: Extensible provider token such as openai, ollama, or koru.

AgentModelsResponse.description:
The models one local agent lists, in the agent's own ids. Empty when the
agent lists none: the picker then shows no model level under it.

id.description: The id the agent itself takes, e.g. `deepseek/v4-pro`.

group.description: The agent's grouping of it — OpenCode's provider, Codex's one group.

agent_working_folder.description:
The folder a local agent works in for this chat, absolute; `None` is
the person's home folder. Only an `agent-*` chat sets it, before its
first message, and a branch copies it.

reasoning_control.description:
What the chat's current model offers as an effort control, so the
chip can read and set it; `None` where the model advertises none.

FeedbackEventId.description: FeedbackEventId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

UpdateChatFolderRequest.description:
The folder a chat's local agent works in. `None` returns the chat to
the home-folder default. Accepted only on an `agent-*` chat with no
message yet: the agent starts in the folder, so a later change would
name a folder the conversation is not in.

UsageTotals.description:
Content-free aggregate measurements for one usage scope or reporting row.

Provider token fields remain optional so an unavailable measurement cannot
be mistaken for a reported zero. Context counts and bytes are measured by
Koru itself and therefore have exact zero values.

UsageGroup.description:
One row in the all-usage report. Every dimension is content-free and can
survive history deletion without retaining a chat or message identity.

replace_pinned_documents.description:
When true, existing pinned documents are ignored and only the explicit
refs are used as context for this turn. Used by the contextual AI pane,
where the current document should replace prior context.

DocumentExportId.description: DocumentExportId — a client-minted UUID v4, never derived from content or location.

system_prompt_override.description:
Debug-only, per-request replacement for Koru's bundled system prompt.
Empty or omitted keeps the versioned bundled prompt.

replace_pinned_documents.description:
When true, existing pinned documents are ignored and only the explicit
refs are used as context for this turn. Used by the contextual AI pane,
where the current document should replace prior context.

ToolDecisionRequest.description:
The optional body of an approve or deny. A local agent offers its own
choices for a permission request; the chosen one's id comes back here.
A workspace tool offers none and takes no body. An agent's row with no
choice is refused, so two same-intent choices can never collapse.

code.description:
A stable code from `koru_artifact_core::ArtifactError::code`, an
authority refusal (`koru_artifact_core::AuthorityRefusal::code`), or
one of the gateway's own: `forbidden`, `artifacts_unavailable`,
`payload_too_large`, `invalid_request`.

message.description:
Safe developer-facing detail. Never a title, a filename or a
principal.

ArtifactFailure.description:
The one failure shape, the same fields as the AI and Store failures so a
gateway client reads every domain's error the same way.

created_by_run.description:
The run whose registration created the family, when an agent did
(D6); `None` when a person created it by hand.

retired_at_ms.description:
Set once, by [`crate::ArtifactRepository::retire_family`]. A retired
family accepts no new version and is left out of the ordinary listing.

ArtifactFamily.description:
One artifact family. Workspace-scoped (D11), titled by a person or by the
run that made it, and **retired rather than deleted**: `retired_at_ms`
is a mark a reader can see and compare, and every version under a retired
family stays readable (PRINCIPLES, *retire state*).

ArtifactTitle.description:
The title a result is named by on a device that cannot open its bytes
(D27). A title is content: it is redacted like the objective.

CreateFamilyRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/families`. The id is the caller's, so a retried
creation is refused as a duplicate rather than made twice.

FamilyResponse.description:
`GET /v1/artifacts/families/{family}`: the family and its versions by
ordinal.

ArtifactVersion.description:
One immutable artifact version.

Identity is `id`; content is `blob`, an address in the workspace's
content-addressed store. The two are separate on purpose: the same bytes
registered twice are two versions with two histories, and a reference to
a version keeps meaning the same thing after the family moves on.
`derived_from` names the version this one was made from, which is how a
provenance walk crosses generations.

Ordinal.description:
A version's place in its family, starting at [`Ordinal::FIRST`]. Assigned
by the store when a version is registered — the next free number under
the family — and unique there (`UNIQUE (family_id, ordinal)`).

MediaType.description:
A `type/subtype` media type, ASCII and lowercased, as the blob store
records it. Not content: it prints in full.

Filename.description:
The name the bytes had where the agent wrote them (D6). Redacted in
`Debug`; shown only by the surface that lists the version.

ProducedBy.description:
Which attempt of which run produced a version. Both halves, because a
run's generation is the fence §7.5 and §7.6 rely on: a late registration
from an older attempt is recorded as that attempt's, not the current one's.

AttemptGeneration.description:
Which attempt of a run is current — the fence §7.5 and §7.6 rely on.

A monotonic counter per run, starting at [`AttemptGeneration::FIRST`]. An
event, an MCP call or a session lookup carrying an older generation may
not touch status, control or authority; see
[`crate::AttemptGeneration::admits`]. It is a counter rather than an id so
"older" is a comparison, not a lookup.

RegisterVersionRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/families/{family}/versions`. Metadata only: the
blob is an address in the family's workspace, already uploaded through
the Store's blob route, and the gateway verifies it is there before the
version exists. The size is the Store's word, not the caller's.

retried.description:
This call found the version an earlier call with the same
registration id had made.

runs.description: Links on the subject and on every ancestor, subject's first.

deleted_runs.description:
**Which of the runs named above no longer exist.**

A person may delete a run and keep what it produced. The result
stays, and its provenance still names the run that made it — so the
sentence has to say *a run that was deleted* rather than print an id
that resolves to nothing. Recorded when the trash is emptied and
read back here; a run absent from this set is simply a run, whether
it belongs to this device or another one.

`#[serde(default)]`, so a walk from a store that predates the set
reads as *none deleted* rather than failing to decode.

Provenance.description:
A version's provenance: the version, every ancestor reached by following
`derived_from` (nearest first), and every run link on any of them.

Three generations read like a sentence: `v3` was produced by run *R2*,
which consumed `v2`, which was derived from `v1`, which run *R1*
produced. P1.13 draws that sentence; this is the fact it draws from.

RunLink.description:
One link between a run and a version. `(run, version, role)` is the key:
a run that reads the same version twice has one input link.

LinkRole.description:
How a run touched a version: read it as an input, or produced it as an
output. A closed domain, `CHECK`ed by the database as well.

LinkRunRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/versions/{version}/runs`: record that a run consumed
or produced the version.

IssueAuthorityRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/authorities`. The run's own workspace, the attempt
this token is for, the grant set as the person left it in the modal
(D28), and the working scope whose `.artifacts/<RunId>/` the tools
accept paths from.

RunWorkspace.description:
The run's working scope on this device. A path is content (standing
requirement 7): it is stored so the gateway can resolve `Register` paths
against it, and it is redacted from every `Debug` rendering.

url.description:
`<gateway base>/v1/runs/<RunId>/mcp` — stable per run across
attempts.

IssuedAuthority.description:
The answer to an issue or an advance: the endpoint the provider is
handed, and the bearer that authenticates this attempt at it. The
bearer is shown nowhere else — not in a later read, not in `Debug`.

AuthorityView.description:
`GET /v1/artifacts/authorities/{run}` and the answer to a revocation:
the record without its token and without its path.

AuthorityState.description:
Whether the authority still stands. A closed domain, `CHECK`ed by the
database as well; a revoked record stays, marked.

AdvanceGenerationRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/authorities/{run}/generation`: the next attempt.
Strictly newer than the current one; the grants are re-read from the
record and cannot be sent.

RunWorkspaceResponse.description:
`GET /v1/artifacts/authorities/{run}/workspace`: **the one answer that
carries the run's working folder back out of the store.**

[`AuthorityView`] deliberately carries no path, and that is still the
rule for every read a surface makes. This is the exception, for the one
caller that needs it: emptying the trash has to remove the folder a
deleted run worked in, and the record is the only durable place that
folder is written down — the scope says what *kind* of folder was asked
for, and only the device that ran it knows which directory that turned
out to be. Re-deriving it from the scope now would name a different
directory whenever a project has moved or a temporary base has been
repointed, which is how a delete removes the wrong thing.

It is behind the **write** scope, not the read one. Reading it is not
what it is for: a person's absolute path leaves this store only into the
hand that is about to delete the folder, and the fence should say so.

Its `Debug` prints no path, like every other type that holds one.

ForgetAuthorityResponse.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/authorities/{run}/forget`: the run was deleted.

The authority record, its grants and its tokens are removed — there is
nothing left for them to authorize — and one row saying the run was
deleted takes their place, so a result the person chose to keep can say
*a run that was deleted* instead of printing an id that resolves to
nothing.

`held_authority` is whether there was a record to remove. `false` is an
ordinary answer, not a failure: a run that never started never had one,
and neither does a run that reached this device by sync.

RunVersionsResponse.description:
`GET /v1/artifacts/runs/{run}/versions`: what a run has registered so
far, oldest first — the hook the orchestrator reads at a turn boundary
(D29) and publishes `delegate.artifact.registered` from.

UnregisteredResponse.description: Every run of the workspace with a folder to look in, newest run first.

unregistered.description:
Files in the folder that are not results, shallowest first then by
path, at most [`MAX_RUN_FOLDER_FILES`].

truncated.description: The folder held more than the scan's bounds allow.

RunFolder.description:
One run's folder, as the surface reads it.

`registered` is how many versions the run has already produced, so D29's
state — *finished having registered nothing* — is a fact the surface can
state rather than infer from an empty list it might simply not have
fetched. `folder_present` separates *the agent wrote nothing* from *the
folder is gone*, which are different sentences.

modified_at_ms.description: The file's modification time, when the filesystem reported one.

UnregisteredFile.description:
One file under a run's `.artifacts/<RunId>/` folder that is **not yet a
result** (D19).

`path` is what [`crate::run_folder::RegisterFileRequest`] echoes back;
`size_bytes` and `modified_at_ms` are what the surface draws beside it.

RelativePath.description:
A file's place **inside** a run's `.artifacts/<RunId>/` folder:
`/`-separated, never absolute, never carrying a parent-directory step.

Content, like a filename, so its `Debug` redacts. It is a *statement of
where to look*, never an authority to look there: the register path rule
(`staging::stage`) still resolves it, walks it for links and proves
containment. Refusing the obvious faults here as well means a listing
this type could not have produced can never be echoed back as a
registration.

RegisterFileRequest.description:
`POST /v1/artifacts/runs/{run}/register` — D19's one click.

The title is optional because the click carries no words: absent, the
file's own last segment names the result, which is what the person is
looking at when they press it.

RegisteredFile.description:
What a Register answers: the version, its family, and whether an
identical earlier registration had already made it.

code.description:
A stable domain code. Run codes include `unknown_run`, `wrong_status`, `not_interrupted`,
`not_delegatable`, `attempt_live`, `prior_attempt_unknown`,
`source_in_trash`, `source_unavailable`, `source_unanswered`,
`context_capture`, `invalid_request`, `forbidden`,
`delegate_unavailable`, and `payload_too_large`. Schedule codes include
`invalid_schedule`, `schedule_conflict`, and `schedule_unavailable`;
transport compatibility may report `delegate_incompatible`.

message.description:
Safe developer-facing detail. Never an objective, a path or a
provider payload.

DelegateFailure.description: The one failure shape, the same fields as the artifact and AI failures.

workspace.description: The workspace the Run document is registered in.

requested_model.description: Explicit model intent. New clients use the v2 create route when present.

grants.description:
The workspaces the run's tools may reach (D28). Empty denies all
workspace access.

CreateRunRequest.description:
`POST /v1/runs`. The client mints the run id, so a retried request is
the same run (§7.1); the executing device is the worker's own and is
not a field a caller supplies.

oneOf.description: A person, as the profile they were acting under.
The delegate worker acting for a run.
The provider agent, as the managed session it ran in.

Objective.description:
What a person asked the agent to do (D9). The one field of a run that
is a prompt, and therefore the one field that must never be reported.

SessionProfileKey.description:
Stable identity for a launch profile. Built-ins remain readable across
machines; user-created profiles are opaque UUIDs.

DelegateModelName.description:
Bounded ASCII model name as a provider reports it — `gpt-5-codex`,
`claude-sonnet-4-5`. Printable ASCII without whitespace, at most 128
bytes. Retained metadata, never an event attribute (§17.3).

oneOf.description: No scope chosen. Refused at admission (P1.5), never started.
The root of a session project.
A folder inside a session project's root.

A directory Koru creates for this run alone and owns (D37 names it:
an unregistered result there survives as long as the run does).

WorkspaceScope.description:
